en: The island province of Camiguin is unique because it has seven volcanoes, which is more volcanoes than the number of its towns.
Taal Volcano features a rare nested structure where Vulcan Point island sits inside a crater lake on Volcano Island in Taal Lake.
The Chocolate Hills in Bohol consist of exactly 1,268 symmetrical cone-shaped mounds that turn brown during the dry season.
Mayon Volcano in Albay is globally renowned for possessing the most perfectly symmetrical and steep volcanic cone in the entire world.
The Verde Island Passage is scientifically recognized as the center of the world's marine shorefish biodiversity, hosting unmatched coral richness.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River is one of the world's longest underground rivers and features a massive cave with its own microclimate.
Laguna de Bay is the largest lake in the Philippines and is so massive that it significantly influences the local climate of Metro Manila.
Mount Apo is the highest peak in the Philippines and serves as the last major refuge for the critically endangered Philippine eagle.
The heart-shaped island province of Marinduque is geographically designated as the exact center of the Philippine archipelago.
The Philippines sits directly on the Pacific Typhoon Belt, causing it to experience an average of 20 tropical cyclones every single year.
The Philippines is one of the most mineral-rich nations globally, holding massive underground reserves of gold, nickel, copper, and chromite.
The Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park is a pristine atoll in the Sulu Sea that is entirely submerged and inaccessible by land.
